summary: 布鲁克林志愿者逐店调查新鲜食物的供应，并画成可查询的网络地图。地图让居民和决策者看见“食物荒漠”，但能否持续更新、是否真正改变购物与政策，还需更多观察。
logic: 把公民绘图用于社区问题
联系低收入区域和健康差距
评估地图的使用和持续维护

paragraphs.brief: 地图标出街区健康食品供应
sentences: Over the last few months, a survey has been carried out of over 200 greengrocers and convenience stores in Crown Heights, a neighborhood in Brooklyn, New York.
过去几个月，研究人员走访了纽约布鲁克林皇冠高地的两百多家果蔬店和便利店。

As researchers from the Brooklyn Food Association enter the details, colorful dots appear on their online map, which display the specific location of each of the food stores in a handful of central Brooklyn neighborhoods.
在布鲁克林食品协会的研究人员输入细节时，他们的在线地图上出现多彩点，显示布鲁克林中部几个街区每个食品商店的具体位置。
Clicking on a dot will show you the store’s name and whether it carries fresh fruit and vegetables, wholegrain bread, low-fat dairy and other healthy options.
点开一个圆点就能看到店名，并了解那里是否出售新鲜蔬果、全麦面包、低脂乳制品等健康食品。
paragraphs.gist: 布鲁克林团队走访皇冠高地两百多家果蔬店和便利店，把地址标在地图上，居民点击圆点即可查看店内是否出售新鲜蔬果等健康食品。

paragraphs.brief: 服务居民寻找食品和政府决策
sentences: The researchers plan eventually to survey the entire borough of Brooklyn.
研究人员计划最终调查整个布鲁克林区
‘We want to get to a more specific and detailed description of what that looks like,’ says Jeffrey Heehs, who leads the project.
项目负责人杰弗里·希斯说：「我们想更具体细致地描述实际的供应情况。」
He hopes it will help residents find fresh food in urban areas where the stores sell mostly packaged snacks or fast food, areas otherwise known as food deserts.
他希望，这能帮助居民在被称为“食物荒漠”的城市片区找到新鲜食物；那里的商店主要售卖包装零食或快餐。
The aim of the project is also to assist government officials in assessing food availability, and in forming future policies about what kind of food should be sold and where.
项目还希望协助政府评估食品的可获得性，为今后决定何地应供应哪些食品提供依据。
paragraphs.gist: 项目打算覆盖整个布鲁克林，既帮食物荒漠里的居民找到新鲜食品，也协助政府判断哪些地区缺少供应、应怎样调整政策。

paragraphs.brief: 公民制图与食品地图趋势交汇
sentences: In fact, the Brooklyn project represents the intersection of two growing trends: mapping fresh food markets in US cities, and private citizens creating online maps of local neighborhood features.
这个项目结合了两种日益兴起的趋势：绘制美国城市的新鲜食品供应地图，以及普通居民自行制作记录街区特色的在线地图。

According to Michael Goodchild, a geographer at the University of California at Santa Barbara, citizen map makers may make maps because there is no good government map, or to record problems such as burned-out traffic lights.
加利福尼亚大学圣巴巴拉分校地理学家迈克尔·古德柴尔德说，民间制图者制作地图，可能是因为政府没有提供合用的地图，也可能是想记录信号灯损坏之类的问题。
paragraphs.gist: 这个项目结合了两股趋势：城市开始绘制新鲜食品分布图，普通居民也动手补足官方地图的空白，记录街区中的具体问题。

paragraphs.brief: 城市地价和郊区超市催生荒漠
sentences: According to recent studies, people at higher risk of chronic disease and who receive minimal incomes for the work they do frequently live in neighborhoods located in food deserts.
根据最近的研究，患慢性病的风险较高，工作收入最低的人往往居住在食物沙漠中的社区。
But how did these food deserts arise?
但是，这些食物沙漠是如何产生的？
Linda Alwitt and Thomas Donley, marketing researchers at DePaul University in Chicago, found that supermarkets often can’t afford the amount of land required for their stores in cities.
芝加哥DePaul大学的营销研究人员Linda Alwitt和Thomas Donley发现超市往往负担不起在城市的商店所需的土地。
City planning researcher Cliff Guy and colleagues at the University of Leeds in the UK found in 2004 that smaller urban groceries tend to close due to competition from suburban supermarkets.
2004年，英国利兹大学的城市规划研究者克利夫·盖伊等人发现，市区的小杂货店往往会因郊区超市的竞争而关闭。
paragraphs.gist: 低收入、慢性病风险高的人常住在食物荒漠；市区土地昂贵让大型超市难以立足，郊区超市的竞争又迫使小杂货店关门。

paragraphs.brief: 新鲜食品不足与健康差距
sentences: As fresh food stores leave a neighborhood, residents find it harder to eat well and stay healthy.
当新鲜食品店离开一个街区时，居民发现很难吃好并保持健康。
Food deserts are linked with lower local health outcomes, and they may be a driving force in the health disparities between lower-income and affluent people in the US.
食物沙漠与当地健康成果较低有关，它们可能是美国低收入者和富裕者之间健康差距的驱动力。
Until recently, the issue attracted little national attention, and received no ongoing funding for research.
直到不久前，这个问题都很少得到全国关注，相关研究也没有持续的经费支持。
paragraphs.gist: 新鲜食品店撤走后，居民更难保持健康饮食，可能加剧贫富群体的健康差距，而这一问题过去既缺全国关注也缺持续的研究经费。

paragraphs.brief: 多城对照商店分布与健康数据
sentences: Now, more US cities are becoming aware of their food landscapes.
如今，更多美国城市开始关注本地的食品供应格局。
Last year, the United States Department of Agriculture launched a map of where food stores are located in all the US counties.
去年，美国农业部发布了一张地图，标示全美各县的食品商店位于何处。

Mari Gallagher, who runs a private consulting firm, says her researchers have mapped food stores and related them to health statistics for the cities of Detroit, Chicago, Cincinnati and Washington, DC.
经营私人咨询公司的玛丽·加拉格尔说，她的团队已绘出底特律、芝加哥、辛辛那提和华盛顿特区的食品店分布，并与各地健康统计资料进行对照。
These maps help cities identify where food deserts are and, occasionally, have documented that people living in food deserts have higher rates of diet-related diseases.
这些地图有助于城市确定食物沙漠的位置，有时还记录了生活在食物沙漠中的人与饮食有关的疾病发病率较高。
paragraphs.gist: 美国农业部及多座城市开始标注食品店位置并与健康统计比较，借此找出食物荒漠，有时也记录到当地饮食相关疾病较多。

paragraphs.brief: 志愿者逐店调查并准备政策建议
sentences: The Brooklyn project differs in that it’s run by a local core of five volunteers who have worked on the project for the past year, rather than trained, academic researchers.
Brooklyn项目不同，由当地五个志愿者组成，他们在过去的一年里一直在该项目上工作，而不是经过培训的学术研究人员。

To gather data, they simply go to individual stores with pre-printed surveys in hand, and once the storekeeper’s permission has been obtained, check off boxes on their list against the products for sale in the store.
收集数据时，他们拿着印好的调查表逐店走访，先征得店主同意，再对照在售商品，在清单上相应的方格内打勾。

Their approach to data collection and research has been made possible by technologies such as mapping software and GPS-related smart phones, Google Maps and OpenStreetMap, an open-source online map with a history of involvement in social issues.
制图软件、带GPS的智能手机、谷歌地图，以及一向关注社会议题的开源在线地图 OpenStreetMap 等技术，使他们能够这样收集数据、开展研究。
Like Brooklyn Food Association volunteers, many citizen online map makers use maps to bring local problems to official attention, Goodchild says.
Goodchild指出，许多公民在线地图制作人使用地图将当地问题引起官方注意：“就像布鲁克林食品协会志愿者一样。”

Heehs, the mapping project leader, says that after his group gathers more data, it will compare neighborhoods, come up with solutions to address local needs, and then present them to New York City officials.
绘图项目负责人希斯说，团队收集到更多资料后，将对各街区进行比较，为当地需求提出解决方案，再提交给纽约市官员。
Their website hasn’t caught them much local or official attention yet, however.
网站尚未引起当地或官方的注意。
It was launched only recently, but its creators haven’t yet set up systems to see who’s looking at it.
网站上线不久，创建者还没建立统计访问者情况的系统。
paragraphs.gist: 布鲁克林项目由五名志愿者逐店征得同意后调查，借电子地图整理数据，准备比较街区并向市府提案，但网站初上线时关注度仍有限。

paragraphs.brief: 价格、易用性及离线可及性
sentences: Experts who visited the Brooklyn group’s site were optimistic but cautious.
访问布鲁克林小组网站的专家虽然乐观，但谨慎。
‘This kind of detailed information could be very useful,’ says Michele Ver Ploeg, an economist for the Department of Agriculture.
Michele Ver Ploeg，农业部的经济学家：“这种详细的资料可能非常有用。”
To make the map more helpful to both residents and policy makers, she would like to see price data for healthy products, too.
为了使地图对居民和决策者都更有帮助，她也希望看到健康产品的价格数据。
Karen Ansel, a registered dietician and a spokesperson for the American Dietetic Association, found the site confusing to navigate.
注册营养师、美国营养学会发言人卡伦·安塞尔发现，网站导航不太容易使用。
‘That said, with this information in place the group has the tools to build a more user-friendly site that could be … very helpful to consumers,’ she says.
她说：「尽管如此，有了这些信息，团队已经具备做出更易用网站的条件，这会对消费者很有帮助。」
‘The group also should ensure their map is available to those who don’t have internet access at home,’ she adds.
她补充说：“这个团体应该确保他们的地图可以提供给那些没有互联网在家里接入的人。”

In fact, a significant proportion of Brooklyn residents don’t have internet access at home and 8 percent rely on dial-up service, instead of high-speed internet access, according to Gretchen Maneval, director of Brooklyn College’s Center for the Study of Brooklyn.
布鲁克林学院布鲁克林研究中心主任格蕾琴·马内瓦尔指出，相当一部分布鲁克林居民家中无法上网，另有 8% 的人只能使用拨号上网，无法通过宽带接入。
‘It’s still very much a work in progress,’ Heehs says of the online map.
Heehs说网上地图：“还在进行中呢。”
They’ll start advertising it online and by email to other community groups, such as urban food garden associations, next month.
下个月，他们将开始在网上宣传，并发电子邮件向城市食物花园协会等其他社区团体介绍网站。
He also hopes warmer days in the spring will draw out fresh volunteers to spread awareness and to finish surveying, as they have about two-thirds of Brooklyn left to cover.
布鲁克林约有三分之二区域还未调查，希斯也希望春日转暖能吸引新志愿者参与宣传并完成走访。
paragraphs.gist: 专家肯定地图的细致资料，也建议补上价格、改善导航并照顾家中不能上网的人；团队还得招募志愿者完成约三分之二地区的调查。

items.en: The online map provides users with a store’s name, ________ and details of its produce.
items.zh: 这张在线地图告诉使用者商店的名称、________，以及所售农产品的详细情况。
items.why: 句中已给“店名"和“是否售卖哪些食品 (即商品详情)”,与之并列缺的就是“具体位置”。

items.en: One goal of the mapping project is to help develop new ________ on food.
items.zh: 这个地图项目的目标之一是帮助制定新的食品________。
items.why: “form…policies”= 制定政策。与题干“develop new…on food"”同义替换。

items.en: Citizen maps are sometimes made when ________ maps are unsatisfactory.
items.zh: 有时，________制作的地图不能满足需要，居民就会自己绘制地图。
items.why: 直接对应“不理想的地图”=“no good government map”.

items.en: New research suggests that people living in food deserts often have low ________.
items.zh: 新研究表明，生活在“食物荒漠”的人往往________偏低。
items.why: 回到对应内容“根据最近的研究，患慢性病的风险较高，工作收入最低的人往往居住在食物沙漠中的社区”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Some supermarkets are unable to buy enough ________ inside cities for their stores.
items.zh: 有些超市在市区买不到足够的________来开店。
items.why: 回到对应内容“芝加哥DePaul大学的营销研究人员Linda Alwitt和Thomas Donley发现超市往往负担不起在城市的商店所需的土地”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Small grocery stores in cities often cannot cope with supermarket ________.
items.zh: 城市里的小型食品店往往难以应对来自超市的________。
items.why: 回到对应内容“2004年，英国利兹大学的城市规划研究者克利夫·盖伊等人发现，市区的小杂货店往往会因郊区超市的竞争而关闭”，再按题干要求写出答案。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

items.en: A group of professional researchers are in charge of the Brooklyn project.
items.zh: 一组专业研究人员负责布鲁克林项目。
items.why: 布鲁克林项目由五名本地志愿者负责，文中明确将他们与受过训练的学术研究人员区分开。

items.en: The Brooklyn project team carries out their assessment of stores without the owner’s knowledge.
items.zh: 布鲁克林项目小组在业主不知情的情况下对商店进行评估。
items.why: 项目人员要先得到店主许可才填写调查表，不能说评估是在店主不知情时进行的。

items.en: The Brooklyn project has experienced technical difficulties setting up the website.
items.zh: 布鲁克林项目在建立网站方面遇到了技术困难。
items.why: 文中只说“尚未设置统计系统”“导航有点混乱”,未说明“遇到技术困难”。无法据此判断为真或假，故NOT GIVEN。

items.en: The city government has taken a considerable interest in the Brooklyn project website.
items.zh: 市政府对布鲁克林项目网站很感兴趣。
items.why: 网站尚未获得多少当地公众或官方关注，与市政府“相当重视”矛盾。

items.en: Michele Ver Ploeg believes the Brooklyn project website should contain additional information.
items.zh: 米歇尔·韦尔·普卢格认为，布鲁克林项目的网站还应提供其他信息。
items.why: 弗普勒格希望地图增加健康食品的价格数据，正是要求网站补充信息。

items.en: The rate of internet use in Brooklyn is unlikely to increase in the near future.
items.zh: 布鲁克林的互联网使用率在近期内不大可能增加。
items.why: 文中仅陈述当前现状，未对“未来是否会上升" 作出预测，故 NOT GIVEN。

items.en: Jeffrey Heehs would like more people to assist with the Brooklyn project research.
items.zh: 杰弗里·希斯希望有更多人协助布鲁克林项目开展调查。
items.why: 希斯希望天气转暖能吸引新志愿者来宣传并调查其余街区，表明他希望有更多帮手。

pairs: 第 7 段 · 第 1 句
第 3 段 · 第 2 句
points: 布鲁克林项目由五名本地志愿者负责，文中明确将他们与受过训练的学术研究人员区分开。
直接对应“不理想的地图”=“no good government map”.
clauses: According to Michael Goodchild, a geographer at the University of California at Santa Barbara, citizen map makers may make maps ….
连接词 because 引出“because there is no good government map, or to record problems such as burned-out traffic lights”，说明主句的原因关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 because 把这一层关系补进去。
Linda Alwitt and Thomas Donley, marketing researchers at DePaul University in Chicago, found ….
“that supermarkets often can’t afford the amount of land required for their stores in cities”补足 found 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 found 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
lead: Ordinary citizens have been using the internet to draw attention to the lack of healthy eating options in inner cities.
普通市民借助互联网，让更多人关注城市中心区缺乏健康饮食选择的问题。
vocabulary: 难以买到新鲜健康食品的地区
